evidence.note: Iteratively resized model (54M→35M→32.5M params) each time measured compressed size exceeded the 32MB cap — reasoned single-lever size adjustments re-checked against the constraint.
Diagnosed torch.compile crash as missing C compiler (root cause), removed compile and added bf16 AMP rather than blindly retrying.

Diagnosed that trained int8 weights compress worse than random (checkpoint grew past 32MB during training); tested lzma/zstd/brotli and switched zlib→lzma to buy ~5MB of capacity within the cap — trading the quantization/compression scheme against model size.
Detected the val_bpb metric was bits-per-token not bits-per-byte; computed bytes/token=3.87 and corrected the true target (val_loss<2.635), updating its design model from evidence.
Diagnosed ~3.3MB torch.save pickle overhead and switched to a raw-binary checkpoint format — a compounding correction buying more headroom under the byte cap.
Killed the 22-layer run creeping toward 32MB at step 7500 and redesigned a 19-layer/29.3M model with 6.75MB size headroom to enable longer training — explicit depth-vs-size-vs-bpb frontier reasoning.

Compute churn against the high anchor: a buggy resume-from-checkpoint detour, then a from-scratch restart that accidentally overwrote the best checkpoint — sinking compute rather than cleanly abandoning dead ends.

In the final run, val_loss plateaued ~2.76 above the 2.635 target; the agent made no new lever change, repeatedly asserting the target was 'reachable in ~X more steps' and submitted a non-passing model (val_bpb~1.026) while training still ran.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly diagnosed the binding constraint from evidence — size cap, compressibility of trained weights, pickle overhead, a wrong bpb metric, and capacity-vs-headroom — and changed the right lever each time, notably trading the compression/serialization scheme (zlib→lzma→raw binary) and depth (22→19 layers) against the byte cap to buy accuracy; this is a clear match to anchor 8. It reaches toward 10 by using each falsified run to update its design model with compounding corrections, but it stops short: it churned compute on a buggy resume path and self-inflicted a best-checkpoint overwrite, and in the end failed to make any principled correction on the bpb plateau, submitting an above-target model. That mix of strong, correct-lever adaptation with wasteful churn and an unclosed bpb gap places it solidly at 8.
